text: If it is argued that in such a situation, even if it is held to be so, the doubt of deviation is difficult to avoid, then it may be replied thus: The doubt of this kind—that the effect might arise even without a cause—is removed because it is superseded by the possibility of obstacles. For one should only entertain a doubt in a case where, in the absence of such doubt, obstacles and the like would not occur. This has been stated as: "Doubt is limited by obstacles" (Nyāya-Kutūhala, Sūtra 3/7).
